setup_summary.text: DIS reports fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-11-17 before the open. Consensus is EPS $1.70 and revenue $25.48B, against $0.73 and $22.46B a year earlier. That implies +13.4% revenue growth and +132% EPS growth.
Fiscal 2026 is a 53-week year with the extra week reported in Q4. Q4 is therefore a 14-week quarter against a 13-week comparison, and management's full-year segment guidance excludes that week.

Q3 FY26 (June quarter) revenue was $25.25B, up 6.8%. Total segment operating income was $5.56B, up 21.4%. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.51 against $2.92, because the prior-year quarter included a $3.3B non-cash Hulu tax benefit.

Q3 segment operating income: Experiences $3,017M (+20%), Entertainment $1,680M (+64%), Sports $858M (-17%). Experiences was a record, while Sports was squeezed by programming costs, including NBA rights-cost timing that shifted costs into Q3.

Q3 GAAP EPS carried $0.55 of after-tax adverse items (A+E impairment and acquisition amortization). Prior-year Q3 carried a net +$1.31 of items, including a $1.56 Hulu tax benefit. GAAP year-on-year EPS comparisons are therefore distorted.

Nine-month operating cash flow was $12.52B (-8.2%). Free cash flow was $5.74B against $7.52B, as capex rose 11% and deferred wildfire-relief tax payments were made. Buybacks were $7.2B over nine months and borrowings rose to $46.0B from $42.0B.
The options market implies a +/-7.3% move, against a +/-6.0% average over the last eight reports. DIS has beaten EPS in each of the last four quarters by an average of 5.5%.

The stock is $110.94 against a consensus price target of $125.67 (+13.3%). Recent analyst actions (Citigroup, Needham, Raymond James) all maintained Buy or Outperform ratings. Whisper EPS is not available.

last_reported.text: Q3 FY26 revenue was $25.25B, +6.8% y/y, including roughly 2 points of service-revenue lift from the Fubo and NFL transactions.

consensus.text: Consensus is $25.48B, implying +13.4% y/y against $22.46B in Q4 FY25.

view.text: Consensus growth of 13.4% is roughly double Q3's 6.8%, but the extra week adds about 7.7% on simple 14/13 pro-rata (my arithmetic). That leaves roughly 5% underlying growth, below Q3 even with Fubo/NFL tailwinds, so the revenue bar does not look demanding if the extra week is fully in the numbers. Risk: parks revenue is seasonally light in late September, so the extra week may be worth less than pro-rata, and the Asia consumer is soft.

metrics_to_model.metric: Diluted EPS (GAAP vs adjusted basis unclear)

last_reported.text: Q3 FY26 GAAP diluted EPS was $1.51, including $0.55 of adverse items. Excluding them it would be about $2.06 (derived). Q4 FY25 GAAP EPS was $0.73.

consensus.text: Consensus EPS is $1.70. The sources do not say whether it is adjusted or GAAP.

view.text: The +132% implied growth compares a likely adjusted consensus with a GAAP base, so it overstates the real step-up. If consensus is adjusted, it is well below the roughly $2.06 ex-items Q3 run-rate, which is consistent with Q4 being seasonally weaker for parks, so the bar looks beatable. A beat is also supported by the 4-for-4 record, and applying the 5.5% average surprise gives about $1.79 (my arithmetic). Q4 may include further impairments or an A+E sale impact below the line.

last_reported.text: Q3 Experiences OI was $3,017M (+20%) on revenue of $9,968M (+10%). It included about $100M of tariff refunds that will not repeat. Nine-month OI was $8,941M (+10%).

view.text: FY25 Experiences OI was $9,995M and the 9M FY25 figure was $8,117M, so Q4 FY25 was $1,878M (derived). Guidance of the high end of high-single-digit full-year growth, excluding the 53rd week, implies FY26 OI of about $10.8-11.0B. That means Q4 OI of roughly $1.85-2.05B, or about -1% to +9% y/y, versus +20% in Q3. This looks conservative unless Asia softness and cost timing are large. Growth inside the 53rd week is on top.

last_reported.text: Q3 global guests were +4%. Domestic attendance was +3% with per-capita spending +4%. International attendance was flat with per-capita spending +7%. Domestic hotel occupancy was 91% against 86%, while international occupancy was 85% against 87%.

view.text: Management says Walt Disney World and cruise forward bookings are healthy, but it flagged a weaker consumer in Shanghai and Hong Kong that continues into Q4. Listen for the international attendance trend and the effect of the new targeted discount programs (after-2pm pricing, Anaheim resident pricing) on per-capita spending.

last_reported.text: Q3 Sports OI was $858M (-17%) and nine-month OI was $1,701M (-14%). Programming and production costs rose 10% in Q3, helped along by NBA rights-cost timing, partly offset by the absence of UFC costs.

view.text: Q4 FY25 Sports OI was $911M (derived from $2,882M for FY25 less $1,971M for 9M). The CFO said the segment is 'growing' on full-year guidance excluding the 53rd week. If that means FY26 above $2,882M, Q4 would need roughly $1.18B or more, about +30% y/y, which looks demanding given the nine-month trend. The metric behind 'growing' is unclear and needs clarifying.

metrics_to_model.metric: Entertainment operating income and SVOD margin

last_reported.text: Q3 Entertainment OI was $1,680M (+64%), driven by subscription and affiliate fees (+12%), lower film impairments and lower marketing. SVOD operating margin was 13%.

view.text: Q4 FY25 Entertainment OI was $691M (derived from $4,674M for FY25 less $3,983M for 9M), an easy comparison. Management still guides double-digit SVOD margin for FY26 excluding the 53rd week. Offsets are weaker advertising (Q3 advertising -1%, rates -4%), SVOD ad pricing pressure, and theatrical underperformance by Mandalorian and Grogu and live-action Moana. Toy Story 5 has passed $1B.

last_reported.text: Q3 buybacks were 17M shares for about $1.7B (average $100.74). Diluted shares were 1,743M in Q3, and 1,726.7M were outstanding on July 29.

view.text: A target of 'at least $9B' against $7.245B repurchased over nine months implies Q4 buybacks of about $1.76B or more (derived). That is a modest tailwind to the EPS share count, though the stock is now about $111 against roughly $100 average in Q3.

last_reported.text: Nine-month capex was $6.78B (+11%) and free cash flow was $5.74B against $7.52B.

view.text: FY26 capex of about $9B implies Q4 capex of about $2.2B (derived). Content spend of about $24B is guided for the year. Higher Experiences depreciation (Q3 +16%) from the cruise fleet is a margin headwind to track.

guidance.guidance: High end of the prior high-single-digit growth range, excluding the 53rd week

claim.text: Management guided Experiences OI growth to the high end of its prior high-single-digit range for FY26, excluding the 53rd week. The CFO said tariffs are not the driver because refunds offset first-half tariff costs.
Q3 SVOD margin was 13% and management remains on track for double-digit SVOD margin in fiscal 2026, excluding the 53rd week impact.

An analyst question states that double-digit adjusted EPS growth for FY26 and FY27 was reaffirmed, and management did not dispute it. The management wording and the adjusted-EPS base are not in the sources.
The buyback target rose to at least $9B from about $7B, largely because cash set aside for the OpenAI deal was freed up and A+E sale proceeds are expected. The 10-K had targeted $7B.
FY26 spend on produced and licensed content including sports rights is expected at about $24B, against $23B in FY25.
FY26 capex is guided to about $9B, against $8B in FY25, on higher Experiences spend partly offset by lower cruise-fleet spend.

guidance.guidance: 'Growing' on full-year guidance excluding the 53rd week; no number given

claim.text: The CFO said Sports is growing on the full-year guidance that excludes the 53rd week, without stating a metric or a number. This is hard to square with nine-month Sports OI of -14% unless Q4 steps up sharply.

guidance.guidance: Roughly nil for the full year; about $100M refund in Q3, little if any in Q4

claim.text: About $100M of tariff refunds hit Experiences OI in Q3. The costs were incurred in the first half, so the full-year effect is about zero.

since_filing.text: Leadership has changed since the 10-K, which listed Robert Iger as CEO. On the Q3 call, Josh D'Amaro speaks as CEO with about five months in the role. The call is the newer source on this point.

The buyback target was raised from about $7B in the 10-K to at least $9B in the 10-Q and call. The securities class action trial date moved from August 17, 2027 (10-K) to November 16, 2027 (10-Q), and derivative complaints grew to ten.

The 10-Q added new carriage and regulatory risk items. NFL Network and NFL RedZone were removed from Comcast Xfinity in Q3 and not reinstated. The FCC ordered early license renewals for all owned stations, filed May 28, with a response pending.

Comcast beat Q3 estimates on 2026-10-22 despite headwinds in its theme parks business, while its Peacock turned a profit for the second time. This is a read-through on the competitive parks and streaming backdrop, with limited detail in the snippet.

Netflix reported Q3 on 2026-10-20/21, beating on EPS but lowering its 2026 advertising revenue forecast to about $2.7B and guiding to slower growth next quarter. This is a read-through on streaming ad-supply and pricing pressure that management flagged for Disney's SVOD ad sales.

On 2026-10-28 the LA Times reported Disney is laying off 100-200 people in the Experiences division, stemming from a regular evaluation of priorities, investments and project timelines, per an unnamed source. This is small, but it could signal timing changes in project spend, and it sits alongside management's pledge of 'meaningful reductions' in labor and SG&A costs.
On 2026-10-20 Disney named Carol Choi Asia Pacific president as Luke Kang retires. Asia is where management flagged consumer weakness in its Shanghai and Hong Kong parks.

key_debates.question: Can Experiences sustain strong growth into Q4 and FY27 despite softer Asia, discounting and tougher comparisons?

bull.text: Q3 Experiences OI grew 20% with global guests +4%, domestic attendance +3% and per-capita spending +4%. Forward bookings at Walt Disney World and Disney Cruise Line are healthy, and management is guiding to the high end of its range. Management attributes growth to its own actions rather than a snapback from last year's Epic Universe opening.

bear.text: Guidance implies Q4 OI of roughly -1% to +9%, a sharp slowdown from Q3, and Q3 included about $100M of non-repeating tariff refunds. The Shanghai and Hong Kong weakness continues into Q4, and new targeted discounts have launched. International attendance was flat, and Experiences depreciation is up 16% on the cruise build-out.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Experiences OI against the roughly $1.85-2.05B implied range, per-capita spending and international attendance, and FY27 commentary on bookings and pricing versus volume.

key_debates.question: Is streaming profitability on a durable path given ad-pricing pressure and a mixed film slate?

bull.text: SVOD margin reached 13% in Q3, with double-digit guided for the year. The Trio bundle and Disney+/Hulu/HBO Max bundle show markedly lower churn, and app unification and the TikTok deal aim to lift engagement. Ad commitments in the upfront rose double digits.

bear.text: Entertainment advertising revenue fell 1% in Q3, with rates down 4%. Management acknowledges supply-driven pricing pressure in SVOD ads, and Netflix just cut its ad forecast. Mandalorian and Grogu and live-action Moana underperformed at the box office.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Entertainment OI against the easy $691M comparison, SVOD margin and ad-revenue growth, and any commentary on subscriber trends, which the filings do not provide.

key_debates.question: Will Sports earnings turn around after double-digit declines?

bull.text: Sports volumes in the upfront were up low teens and Super Bowl inventory is sold out. The NBA Finals and NHL playoffs drew record viewership, effective rates are rising 5-6%, and NBA cost timing pulled costs into Q3.

bear.text: Sports OI fell 17% in Q3 and 14% over nine months as programming costs rose 10% on contractual escalators and new rights. Nine-month affiliate fees were hit by 3% fewer subscribers and a carriage suspension, and the NFL Network is off Comcast Xfinity.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Sports OI against the $911M comparison, the clarified FY26 Sports guidance, and the status of the NFL Network carriage dispute.

key_debates.question: How much is the earnings bar distorted by the 53rd week and GAAP-versus-adjusted accounting?

bull.text: The extra week mechanically adds about 7.7% to the quarter. Consensus revenue growth of 13.4% therefore implies only about 5% underlying growth, and the company has beaten four of four quarters.

bear.text: Management guides ex-53rd week, and the sources do not size the extra week. The consensus basis is unknown, and Q3 showed GAAP can diverge sharply from adjusted through impairments and tax items. A+E sale accounting and any new impairments could hit GAAP again.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Company disclosure of the 53rd-week contribution and the adjusted-versus-GAAP reconciliation in the earnings release.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: A clean beat above the 5.5% average surprise. Experiences OI lands at the top of the implied range or above, with the extra week an additional lift. SVOD margin is at or above 13%, Sports shows improvement, and management sets a confident FY27 double-digit EPS framework with more buyback capacity. The stock moves up through the +/-7.3% implied range.

triggers: Experiences Q4 OI above about $2.0B excluding the extra week
Ad commentary stable or improving despite supply
FY27 EPS guided at or above double-digit growth

scenarios.name: base

description.text: A modest EPS beat to around $1.75-1.80 and revenue near $25.5B, in line with the beat record. Experiences grows low-to-mid single digits excluding the extra week, while Entertainment grows off an easy comparison. Sports is flat to down, and the outlook is reiterated with some caution on Asia and advertising. The stock moves within about +/-6%.

triggers: Full-year Experiences OI lands at the high end of its range

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: The beat is driven by below-the-line items while the core disappoints. Asia weakness spreads or discounting dilutes per-capita spending. Sports costs stay heavy and SVOD ad pricing softens, and FY27 commentary is cautious or lacks specifics. Impairments or A+E-sale effects hit GAAP. A move beyond the -7.3% implied range is possible.

triggers: Experiences Q4 OI at or below the low end of the implied range
Domestic per-capita spending growth slows from +4% or international attendance turns negative
Sports OI down again with no guidance clarity
Weaker SVOD advertising revenue or margin below double-digit pace

claim.text: Asia consumer weakness in Shanghai and Hong Kong parks started in Q3 and is continuing in Q4.
SVOD ad-pricing pressure from rising market supply, as Netflix's lowered ad forecast also signals.
Carriage disputes and blackouts: NFL Network and RedZone are off Comcast Xfinity, YouTube TV was temporarily dropped in Q1, and further renewals expire in fiscal 2026.
The FCC ordered early renewal of all owned-station licenses; the filing was made May 28 and a response is pending.
Sports rights escalators and a theatrical slate that can be volatile (Toy Story 5 over $1B against disappointing Mandalorian and Moana) weigh on earnings quality.

Litigation: the securities class action (trial now November 2027) and ten derivative suits. The DISH antitrust counterclaims were stayed pending DISH's bankruptcy, and the Unger motion to compel arbitration is pending.
The capex ramp and cruise fleet expansion pressure depreciation (Experiences +16% in Q3) and free cash flow, while borrowings rose about $4B in nine months to fund buybacks and capex.

Guild and union contracts, some of which were due to expire in fiscal 2026, create work-stoppage risk. Separately, Experiences layoffs of 100-200 people reported on 2026-10-28 may signal project-timing changes.
Macro and fuel exposure: the CFO said fuel impact is minimal thanks to hedging and efficiency, but consumer weakness in telecom, restaurant and CPG ad categories is evident.

questions_for_management.question: How much revenue and operating income does the 53rd week contribute by segment, and does the double-digit FY26 and FY27 adjusted EPS framework include or exclude it?

why.text: Q4 is a 14-week quarter but all segment guidance excludes the extra week, which makes consensus comparisons and the 13.4% implied revenue growth hard to interpret.

questions_for_management.question: Why does high-end Experiences guidance imply a sharp Q4 slowdown from +20% in Q3, and how much of the Asia weakness, pre-opening cost or depreciation drives it?

why.text: FY25 Experiences OI of $9,995M and 9M FY26 of $8,941M mean the guided range implies Q4 OI of roughly -1% to +9%.

questions_for_management.question: What does 'growing' mean for Sports in FY26, and what Q4 Sports OI does it imply against $911M last year?

why.text: Nine-month Sports OI is down 14%, and the CFO's comment cannot be reconciled without a large Q4 step-up.

questions_for_management.question: What is the current state of SVOD ad pricing and sell-through, and does the 13% Q3 margin hold through Q4?

why.text: Entertainment advertising fell 1% in Q3 with rates down 4%, management cited supply-driven pricing pressure, and Netflix cut its ad forecast.

questions_for_management.question: How large is the planned cost reduction in labor and SG&A, when does it land, and how does it relate to the reported Experiences layoffs and project timing?

why.text: The CFO flagged 'meaningful reductions' without sizing them, and the LA Times reported cuts tied to project timelines.

questions_for_management.question: What is the timeline and expected accounting for the A+E sale (roughly $1.2B), and does any other write-down remain at risk?

why.text: A+E impairments totaled $959M year to date, and closing is expected by fiscal year-end, which affects Q4 GAAP and the buyback funding.

questions_for_management.question: What is the plan for the NFL Network carriage dispute with Comcast and the FCC license-renewal process, and what is the financial exposure?

why.text: Both are new 10-Q risk items with no quantification.
